state: A homeowner hears rattling in the walls at night and suspects rats.

options.text: Seal every hole with poison inside the walls.
Set snap traps along runs and seal entry holes after.
Ignore it until spring.

reference.rationale_short: Poison in walls means dead rats in walls; traps plus sealing breaks the cycle.

state: A job seeker is asked to do a three-day unpaid 'trial project' before hiring.

options.text: Do the full project for free to prove yourself.
Offer a two-hour paid sample or references instead.
Refuse all trial tasks on principle.

reference.rationale_short: Three unpaid days is spec work, not a trial; a short sample proves skill without exploitation.

state: A cyclist is offered a used carbon frame with a visible crack near the seat tube.

options.text: Buy it cheap and ride carefully.
Walk away; cracked carbon fails without warning.
Wrap it in tape and use it for commuting.

reference.rationale_short: Carbon does not bend, it snaps; a seat-tube crack is a crash waiting at speed.

state: A renter's deposit of two months is withheld over 'cleaning' with no invoice.

options.text: Accept the loss and move on.
Demand an itemised invoice and dispute in writing.
Sue the landlord immediately.

reference.rationale_short: No invoice means no proof of cost; a written dispute forces either evidence or refund.

state: A parent's 10-year-old wants a smartphone 'because everyone has one'.

options.text: Buy the latest model to fit in.
Start with a basic phone plus clear screen-time rules.
Ban phones until sixteen.

reference.rationale_short: A basic phone teaches responsibility gradually; a flagship feeds pressure, a ban feeds secrecy.

state: A tourist's flight is cancelled; the airline offers a voucher instead of a refund.

options.text: Take the voucher to avoid hassle.
Insist on the cash refund the regulation guarantees.
Buy a new ticket and abandon the claim.

reference.rationale_short: Cancelled-flight refunds are a legal right, not a favour; vouchers expire, cash does not.

state: A novice investor is pitched crypto doubling money in a month, 'guaranteed'.

options.text: Invest life savings immediately.
Walk away; guaranteed doubles are fraud by definition.
Borrow to invest bigger.

reference.rationale_short: Guaranteed high returns violate arithmetic; the only winning move is refusal.

state: A colleague asks to 'borrow' your login to check something quickly.

options.text: Share it since you trust them.
Decline and help them through their own account.
Share it then change the password later.

reference.rationale_short: Shared logins destroy the audit trail; helping via their account keeps both safe.

state: A homeowner's basement floods at 2am during heavy rain.

options.text: Wait until morning to call anyone.
Cut power to the basement, move valuables up, call emergency services.
Wade in to save boxes in the dark.

reference.rationale_short: Water plus electricity kills in the dark; power off first, boxes are replaceable.

state: A student considers buying an essay online for a final paper.

options.text: Buy it; everyone does it.
Write it, ask the tutor for an extension if needed.
Copy from a friend instead.

reference.rationale_short: Contract cheating risks expulsion and teaches nothing; an extension request is free and honest.

state: A driver is tailgated aggressively on a two-lane road at night.

options.text: Brake-check the tailgater.
Ease off, let them pass at the next safe spot.
Speed up to lose them.

reference.rationale_short: Ego manoeuvres at night kill; yielding costs seconds, brake-checks cost bumpers.

state: A flatmate eats others' food from the shared fridge repeatedly.

options.text: Eat their food in revenge.
Label food and agree house rules at a flat meeting.
Move out immediately.

reference.rationale_short: Labels plus agreed rules end fridge wars; revenge eating escalates, moving out over snacks is overkill.

state: A pensioner is offered a 'free' medical device, only postage of 50 to pay.

options.text: Pay the postage since the device is free.
Decline and report the offer as a subscription trap.
Order three while they last.

reference.rationale_short: Postage-first 'free' offers harvest card details for recurring charges; reporting protects others.

state: A manager must choose between two suppliers: cheapest with no warranty or pricier with a 5-year warranty.

options.text: Take the cheapest to save the quarter.
Take the warranted one and document total cost of ownership.
Delay the purchase indefinitely.

reference.rationale_short: Unwarranted savings evaporate at the first failure; total cost beats sticker price.

state: A teenager receives compliment messages from an unknown number asking for photos.

options.text: Reply politely since they are nice.
Do not reply, block, and tell parents.
Send a photo without a face.

reference.rationale_short: An unknown adult seeking a teen's photos is a grooming pattern; blocking plus parents immediately.

state: A developer finds a critical bug on Friday evening before a Monday release.

options.text: Hotfix straight to production now.
Patch on staging, run tests, deploy with review.
Hide the bug until after release.

reference.rationale_short: Friday-night cowboy deploys cause Monday outages; staging plus review is hours, not days.

state: A diner finds a foreign object in their drink.

options.text: Drink it to avoid a scene.
Return it and ask for a replacement, alert staff calmly.
Smash the glass and demand free drinks all night.

reference.rationale_short: A calm return gets a fresh drink and fixes the line; theatrics get security.

state: A company laptop with customer data is stolen from a car.

options.text: Hope the thief only wants hardware.
Report to IT for remote wipe and start breach procedure.
Buy a replacement quietly.

reference.rationale_short: Customer data on the move is a breach until wiped; hope is not a security control.

state: A gym trainer pushes a client to lift beyond safe form for a video.

options.text: Lift it for the camera.
Refuse and switch to a trainer who respects form.
Lift it but skip the video.

reference.rationale_short: Form failure under load injures spines; a trainer chasing content over safety gets replaced.

state: A neighbour's dog barks all night; talks failed.

options.text: Poison the dog's food.
File a noise complaint with logged nights.
Buy earplugs and suffer.

reference.rationale_short: Logged complaints trigger enforcement; harming the animal is a crime, earplugs surrender.

state: A student tenant's boiler breaks in December; the landlord stalls for weeks.

options.text: Buy heaters and pay the bill yourself.
Send a written repair deadline, then arrange repair and deduct.
Withhold all rent immediately.

reference.rationale_short: Heat is a habitability right; a written deadline then deduct-and-repair follows the legal path.

state: A driver puts diesel in a petrol car, realising after 5 litres.

options.text: Top up with petrol to dilute and drive on.
Do not start the engine, tow to a garage for a flush.
Start it to see if it runs.

reference.rationale_short: Diesel destroys pump and injectors once the engine turns; not starting saves the engine.

state: A couple inherits a house with a mortgage; the bank wants a decision in 30 days.

options.text: Sign the acceptance without reading.
Get the debt report and a lawyer's advice first.
Reject the inheritance immediately.

reference.rationale_short: A mortgaged inheritance can be debt, not wealth; lawyer and report before signature.

state: A babysitter is offered cash to keep quiet about a parent's affair.

options.text: Take the cash and stay quiet.
Refuse the money and stay out of the marriage.
Tell the other parent for a bigger payout.

reference.rationale_short: Paid silence makes the sitter leverage in a divorce; refusal keeps the job and conscience.

state: A cyclist rides at night with no lights on an unlit road.

options.text: Ride on the pavement to be safe.
Fit lights before riding; walk until then.
Ride fast so cars notice.

reference.rationale_short: Invisible means hittable; lights are cheap, pavement riding endangers walkers.

state: A flat owner wants to rent to tourists without registering the business.

options.text: Rent cash-in-hand like everyone does.
Register and price the tax into the rate.
Stop renting entirely.

reference.rationale_short: Unregistered rentals draw fines larger than the tax; legal rates are a business cost.

state: A nurse sees a colleague pocketing medication from the dispensary.

options.text: Ignore it, not your ward.
Report through the hospital's incident channel.
Confront the colleague in front of patients.

reference.rationale_short: Drug diversion endangers patients; the incident channel protects the reporter, scenes protect no one.

state: A shopkeeper's supplier demands cash upfront for the whole season's stock.

options.text: Pay everything upfront for the discount.
Pay half now, half on delivery with a receipt.
Find another supplier without negotiating.

reference.rationale_short: Half upfront with a receipt shares risk; full prepayment leaves the buyer without leverage.

state: A student is pressured by friends to shoplift 'for fun'.

options.text: Join in to keep the friends.
Refuse and find friends who do not steal.
Report the friends to the police.

reference.rationale_short: A theft record outlives the friendship; refusal plus distance beats both joining and snitching.

state: A homeowner discovers asbestos tiles during a DIY renovation.

options.text: Rip them out with a dust mask from the shop.
Stop work, seal the area, call a licensed remover.
Tile over them and forget.

reference.rationale_short: Asbestos fibres kill decades later; licensed removal is the only legal and safe path.

state: A driver finds the fuel nozzle will not shut off and petrol spills down the car.

options.text: Keep filling to the top.
Stop, alert the attendant, move the car from the pump.
Wipe it with a rag and drive on.

reference.rationale_short: Spilled fuel at a pump is a fire waiting; stop and attendant, not a rag.

state: A tenant is asked to leave because the landlord's cousin 'needs' the flat.

options.text: Leave immediately without paperwork.
Demand the legal notice period in writing.
Change the locks and stay.

reference.rationale_short: Cousin or not, notice periods are law; written notice buys time to find a flat.

state: A junior employee is told to sign off on safety checks they never performed.

options.text: Sign; the boss takes responsibility.
Refuse to sign what was not checked, in writing.
Sign but tell a colleague.

reference.rationale_short: A signature transfers liability to the signer; refusal in writing keeps it with the boss.

state: A tourist loses a wallet with all documents; the embassy opens tomorrow.

options.text: Try crossing the border without documents.
Report to police, get a certificate, wait for the embassy.
Borrow a fellow traveller's passport.

reference.rationale_short: A police loss certificate unlocks an embassy travel document; a borrowed passport is a crime.

state: A child finds a box of pills and asks to try the 'candy'.

options.text: Give one to taste.
Move pills out of reach and explain they are not candy.
Hide the box without explaining.

reference.rationale_short: Pills out of reach plus an explanation; hiding without explaining leaves curiosity.

state: A worker is offered Sunday shifts with no day off in return.

options.text: Accept Sundays for everyone.
Accept voluntarily with a bonus and rotation.
Reject Sundays entirely.

reference.rationale_short: Voluntary Sundays with a bonus fill shifts without losing staff; compulsion drives resignations.

state: A patient is asked for informal payment to skip a surgery queue.

options.text: Pay since health comes first.
Decline, stay in queue, report the request.
Decline and wait without reporting.

reference.rationale_short: Paying buys a place but feeds the queue-selling; reporting plus waiting is the only clean path.

state: A landlord keeps the deposit over 'cleaning' with no invoice.

options.text: Accept the loss and move on.
Demand an itemised invoice and dispute in writing.
Sue the landlord immediately.

reference.rationale_short: No invoice means no proof of cost; a written dispute forces either evidence or refund.

state: A student's flat has no grounding for a donated set of computers.

options.text: Plug everything in now.
Fix the wiring first, then plug in.
Reject the donation.

reference.rationale_short: Faulty wiring plus twenty machines is a fire risk; the donation waits for the electrician.

state: A beekeeper notices die-off near an orchard sprayed yesterday; the owner claims the spray is harmless.

options.text: Trust the owner's word.
Report the suspicion to the inspectorate.
Move the hives without reporting.

reference.rationale_short: Die-off after spraying is reasonable suspicion; the inspectorate establishes facts.

state: A graduate chooses a faculty: parents push law, they love programming, deadlines in two days.

options.text: Enrol in law for peace.
Enrol in what they love.
Pause a year with no plan.

reference.rationale_short: Four years against one's will cost more than parental displeasure.

state: A buyer considers a 15-year-old car; the seller refuses a test drive.

options.text: Buy it since it is cheap.
Walk away or condition the sale on a mechanic's check.
Pay a deposit so the seller 'holds' it.

reference.rationale_short: Whoever blocks a test drive hides a fault; a mechanic's check or no deal.

state: A tenant's flatmate eats everyone's food from the shared fridge.

options.text: Eat their food in revenge.
Label food and agree house rules together.
Move out immediately.

reference.rationale_short: Labels plus rules end fridge wars; revenge escalates, moving out over snacks is overkill.

state: A developer is told to sign off on safety checks never performed.

options.text: Sign; the boss takes responsibility.
Refuse to sign what was not checked, in writing.
Sign but tell a colleague.

reference.rationale_short: A signature transfers liability to the signer; written refusal keeps it with the boss.

state: A child loses their way in a department store; staff offer to let them search alone.

options.text: Let them search for the parent.
Keep the child at the till and page the parent.
Take them to the car park for visibility.

reference.rationale_short: A lost child is never sent off alone; till plus announcement reunites safely.

state: A school's donated computers arrive but wiring lacks grounding.

options.text: Plug everything in now.
Fix the wiring first, then plug in.
Reject the donation.

reference.rationale_short: Faulty wiring plus twenty machines is a fire risk; the donation waits for the electrician.

state: A worker handles chemicals without a mask because it itches.

options.text: Work unmasked like the rest.
Wear the mask and demand proper protective gear.
Quit the job.

reference.rationale_short: Chemicals poison slowly and surely; gear is a right, not a majority vote.

state: A landlord demands the flat returned to original condition after 5 years.

options.text: Renovate the whole flat at your expense.
Return it clean; normal wear is not damage.
Leave it as is without cleaning.

reference.rationale_short: Normal wear is legally the landlord's cost; cleaning yes, renovation no.

state: A graduate fails the medical school entry exam; parents offer a private school abroad.

options.text: Enrol private since parents pay.
Prepare for a year while working.
Enrol in a field they dislike.

reference.rationale_short: A prep year with work preserves both the dream and the money; private without drive is an expensive mistake.

state: A driver is shouted at by an aggressive fare-dodger on the bus.

options.text: Stop the bus and call the police.
Let the inspector handle it alone.
Throw the passenger out personally.

reference.rationale_short: The driver never leaves the cabin; a police call goes via dispatch while the inspector buys time talking.
